claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you may have.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK. I'm asking because I have a teenager at home and I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context. That's helpful to know you have a teenager at home.

To determine eligibility for a teenager, I need to understand their current situation better.

**How old is your teenager, and are they currently in education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: My teenager, Alex, is 17. Yes, he's still in education - he's doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and in approved education (A-levels), that's a positive factor for eligibility.

**Are you living with Alex, or is Alex living with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, that's helpful. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex's upkeep.

**Are you providing financial support for Alex's living expenses, such as food, clothes, and other necessities?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I provide for all his living expenses - food, clothes, school supplies, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's excellent. Now I need to check one more important thing regarding your income, as this can affect Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year?**

(This is relevant because there may be a tax charge on Child Benefit if either of you earns above this threshold, though you would still be eligible to receive it.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I'm just trying to find out if I'm eligible to claim it in the first place. Does my income affect whether I can actually get Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question. You're right to clarify - your income doesn't actually affect whether you can **claim** Child Benefit in the first place. You would still be eligible to receive it.

However, if you or a partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may have to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit as a tax charge, but that's a separate issue from eligibility.

For now, let me confirm: **Is there anyone else (such as a partner or spouse) who also claims responsibility for Alex, or are you the sole person responsible for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm the sole person responsible for Alex. It's just the two of us.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK ✓
- Alex is 17 and living with you ✓
- Alex is in approved education (A-levels) ✓
- You are providing for all of Alex's living expenses ✓
- You are the sole person responsible for Alex ✓

You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Since Alex is 17 and in approved full-time education, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him. Child Benefit can continue until he reaches 20, provided he remains in approved education or training.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Congratulations! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim for Child Benefit. The process is straightforward, and you should receive guidance from HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) on how to proceed with your application.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
